mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by more than 0.25% in a single month, the expected S&P 500 20-day forward return turns negative due to tightened financing conditions and reduced corporate investment activity.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, 20-day forward returns remain non-negative despite FEDFUNDS exceeding the trigger threshold, or the change in FEDFUNDS is not statistically significant (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer payrolls (PAYEMS < previous + 10,000 and HOUST > previous + 5,000) predicts a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return as labor market weakness outweighs demand signals.
regime_hint: Labor market softening with weak wage growth
failure_condition: In regimes where inflation is also falling, the 60-day forward return is positive or not statistically different from baseline (Granger causality fails).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average signals accelerating business demand, which is associated with a positive S&P 20-day forward return when consumer confidence is also expanding (CPIAUCSL > 225).
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative or insignificant even when INDPRO remains above its 12-month average for at least 4 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: During a sustained period of falling consumer prices (CPIAUCSL < 220 for 3 consecutive months), the S&P 5-day forward return tends to be positive as investors anticipate future rate cuts and demand deflation-adjusted assets.
failure_condition: Over 12 months, the 5-day forward return is never positive when CPIAUCSL remains below 220 for the required period.
